name: areanet/contentfly
description: Contentfly — data storage and core functions as a library. Symfony 7.4, Doctrine ORM 3.

suggest.symfony/ldap: For Classes\Security\LdapProvider — login against LDAP or Active Directory. Deliberately NOT in require: the package requires the system extension ext-ldap, and demanding that from every installation that does not use a directory at all would be the wrong direction (013-005-0004).
suggest.rector/rector: For the migration rule Migration\RemovedAttributeFieldsRector — it converts an existing project's entity directory from annotations to attributes (story 007-002). Deliberately NOT in require: the class is only ever loaded by a rector.php, never at runtime; a production run does not need it.

notes: THIS IS THE FRAMEWORK'S MANIFEST (since 007-001-0004). It carries what lib/
itself uses — and nothing else. Whatever the project needs is in the project's
manifest one level up.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE:
vlucas/phpdotenv   used ONLY by custom/config.php, i.e. the template, i.e. the
project. Counted on 2026-09-11: 0 hits in lib/, 1 in
custom/. Until 007-001-0004 it was here because 'root' and
'framework' were the same manifest.
require-dev        PHPUnit, PHPStan, Rector belong in the repository where
development happens, not in a package someone includes.
Whoever uses a library inherits its require entries, but
not its tools.
config.platform    A library must not dictate a platform version to its
consumer. The setting belongs where installation happens.
config.audit       The gate runs against the project's lock; the exceptions
live there as well.
BEFORE ANYONE TOUCHES THE CONSTRAINTS — the numbers are not chosen but justified.
What forces them has moved twice: until epic 009 Silex and knplabs capped them
from above, after that Doctrine — and since epic 010 nothing caps them from above.
What remains are lower bounds and decisions.
1. symfony/* is at ^7.4 — LTS, bug fixes until Nov 2028, security until Nov 2029.
Deliberately not 8.x: the same features, but PHP >= 8.4 in EVERY environment
and a mandatory minor every 6 months. Reasoning in
an_project/docs/architecture.md, Key decisions, 2026-09-04.
2. doctrine/orm is at ^3 and therefore effectively at 3.7. The jump from ORM 2 came
with epic 010: since then the entities carry PHP attributes instead of
annotations, and doctrine/annotations is out of the tree.
3. doctrine/persistence is at ^3.4 || ^4 — the cap from 007-001-0004 has fallen
(000-000-0031). It is listed although doctrine/orm pulls it in: the framework
uses Doctrine\Persistence\Mapping\Driver\MappingDriverChain directly.
Persistence 4.2 deprecated AbstractClassMetadataFactory::setMetadataFor(), and
Classes/Events/LoadMetadata called it. Measured on a fresh installation, the
call did nothing: the listener changes the metadata in place, and the factory
stores that same instance itself. Without it the same 15 tables carry
modified_index and the schema dump is identical — so the line went, and no
custom ClassMetadataFactory was needed. Both majors are allowed because both
were run: 3.4.5 before the jump, 4.x after it.
4. doctrine/dbal is at ^3.10. The LOWER bound is forced: symfony/http-foundation
7.4 declares a conflict with doctrine/dbal <3.6. The UPPER bound is a decision —
ORM 3.7 requires ^3.8.2 || ^4, so DBAL 4 would be allowed. Whoever wants it
checks it as a separate step.
The chain is shorter than it used to be: nothing caps from above any more. Whoever
changes one of the three lines still checks the other two along with it.
THE VERSION IS NOT HERE, AND THAT IS THE POINT (011-002-0003). Until then this
manifest carried a `version` field, and version.php carried the same number a
second time. It was there for the `path` repository of the development tree —
without it Composer derives a path package's version from the Git branch.
IT MADE THE DELIVERY IMPOSSIBLE. Composer discards a tag whose composer.json
declares a DIFFERENT version than the tag itself. Measured on 2026-09-17: with
the field the tag v2.0.0 was seen and v2.0.0-rc1 was dropped without a word;
without it, both are seen. A pre-release tag is how this path gets proven before
a release version is decided — so the field went, and the TAG is now the single
source of the delivered version. That is Composer's own recommendation for
packages distributed through a VCS repository.
The development tree keeps its stable version through the path repository's
`options.versions`, one level up — where it belongs: it is a statement about
this checkout, not about the package.
version.php stays. It is what the APPLICATION reads at runtime (APP_VERSION),
and tools/ci/paket-veroeffentlichen.sh checks tag, version.php and the path
option against each other before it publishes — a guarantee nobody checks is
no guarantee.
